data.probe: Refuted: json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode never returns end=0 for a JSON value it decoded -- the shortest JSON value is one character, and raw_decode('{}') returns ({}, 2) -- so the loop always advances and cannot hang. Belt-and-braces: text[first + max(end, 1):] now makes progress provable even under a pathological decoder, and test_a_non_refusal_object_without_a_refusal_is_not_one_and_terminates asserts _refusal('{}') == '' (the exact 'end==0' shape) without hanging.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test locks in the bug it claims to cover. Bbe5f98b150 is that `gate run … unit_tests --timeout 6900` still gives up at `[ci].suite_wait_s` (1800s) because `_run_holding_the_suite_lock` does not pass a `wait_s` override; a regression test must fail on that unfixed path and pass only once `--timeout` extends the suite-lock wait, as Ba5d5d63f12 did for ci. This test calls `_run_holding_the_suite_lock(gdef, tmp_path, Config(), {}, None, 0)` — no `--timeout` argument at all, despite `GateDef(..., timeout_s=6900)` — and asserts `seen == {"wait_s": None}`. On the broken code that assertion succeeds, so `ddflow complete fix-Bbe5f98b150 --regression-test` can close the bug while a 6900s gate run still stops at 1800s; a correct fix that passes `wait_s` derived from 6900 makes this test fail.
